summary: The paths are computed from a real loss function, finite-difference gradients, and momentum. They closely match independently derived analytic paths. They are then replayed, with hard boundaries and different momentum as well as learning rate.

claims.claim: The ball follows negative loss gradients with momentum.
claims.how: All 22 points in each of the three paths agree with analytic-gradient trajectories to absolute error below 0.000006 in position and plotted height.

sources.title: Gradient descent
sources.says: Gradient descent moves against the gradient with a chosen step size; its convergence depends on the objective and step size.

sources.title: Momentum
sources.says: Momentum retains part of previous updates while incorporating the current gradient.

claims.note: Central differences with spacing 0.0001 explain the small numerical error; 22 points make 21 displayed steps.

claims.claim: Momentum carries part of the previous update.
claims.how: The presets use learning rate and momentum pairs 0.035/0.3, 0.17/0.5, and 0.95/0.

sources.title: Momentum
sources.says: Momentum retains part of previous updates while incorporating the current gradient.

claims.claim: The three paths are a limited example of learning-rate effects.
claims.how: The large step is clipped at the walls, and each choice can also change momentum; the graphic is not a guarantee of convergence on arbitrary losses.

simplified: The path is computed once and replayed, not optimized during each tap. Positions are clipped to a fixed square. The learning-rate choices also change momentum, so they are not a controlled comparison of step size alone.

fixes.what: Label both learning rate and momentum, or hold momentum fixed in a future comparison.
